accessibility: The page is one main landmark; the title is the EmptyState title and the document title reads the same title followed by the product name.
The status code and the path are marked not to be translated; the icon is decorative and the title carries the meaning.
Go to Overview keeps its label as its accessible name, a visible 2px primary focus outline and a 44px target on touch tiers.
constraints: Built only from Adapter Widgets (Stack, Text, Button, EmptyState); no Widget outside the Adapter catalog.

The not-found sentence and the requested path are two Text Widgets side by side, because the app writes the path as inline code after a translated sentence; the status code line sits in the action group of the EmptyState Widget, which has no slot beneath its description.
Every visible string is bound with $i18n except identities (the path and the status code); en-US and zh-TW keep identical key sets.
Visual language follows the Quiet Canvas design system in DESIGN.md.
entryConditions: A person opened an address under the Workbench that matches no page (a 404), or the Workbench hit a fatal client error; Nuxt then renders this page in place of its built-in English one. It is not a route, so no entry of the route map names it.
The base state is the not-found page for the address /nowhere; Variants show the unexpected-error page with and without a status code.
The render context selects one Workspace viewport preset, one Locale and one theme; the page is centered on the app surface and replaces the whole Workbench shell, so no sidebar or top bar is shown.
spec.intent: Show the Workbench's own error page (app/error.vue) as built from Adapter Widgets only: what a person sees on an address that has no Workbench page and on a fatal client error, in the Workbench language, with one way back to the Overview.
interactionRules: A 404 names the requested path and the status code literally (neither is translated); any other status shows a generic title and sentence and the status code when the error has one.
The error's own message is never shown, because it is framework English; the page says what happened in the Workbench language only.
Go to Overview is the one action: it clears the error and navigates to the Overview at /.
